title: A Unified Framework for Operator Backpropagation and Observable Measurement in Quantum Computing
abstract: Decoherence imposes severe limits on quantum circuit depth, motivating methods to reduce circuit depth. Operator backpropagation has recently been proposed as a way to lower circuit depth by classically backpropagating observables through subcircuits. While it lowers the circuit depth, it also significantly increases the number of backpropagated observables that must be measured. This calls for an efficient measurement protocol tailored to these backpropagated observables. Moreover, errors arise both during the backpropagation procedure and during measurement, and they accumulate in the final computation. No prior work has examined how to integrate operator backpropagation with advanced measurement protocols, and how to jointly optimize the combined process.   In this paper, we introduce a comprehensive framework to determine the appropriate measurement protocol to achieve a desired level of accuracy with the fewest number of measurements based on the number of qubit-wise commuting (QWC) groups formed from operator backpropagation. We analyze and categorize the primary sources of error that arise through our workflow, including error incurred from the backpropagation algorithm, truncation error, and shot noise variation. We also examine truncation strategies to reduce the number of backpropagated observables by characterizing the structure of the set of backpropagated observables.
summary: This paper presents a unified framework to optimize the process of estimating quantum expectation values by combining Operator Backpropagation (OBP) with advanced measurement protocols. It systematically determines the most efficient measurement strategy—choosing between QWC grouping or derandomization—by analyzing accumulated errors and resource scaling. This guides the development of more resource-efficient quantum algorithms for NISQ devices.
main_problem: To develop a unified framework that co-optimizes operator backpropagation and observable measurement protocols to achieve a desired accuracy with the minimum number of measurements.
main_result: The optimal measurement strategy depends on a trade-off between Qubit-wise Commuting (QWC) grouping and derandomization, leading to a combined OBP-Derandomization protocol that significantly improves efficiency over individual methods.
method: The authors propose a framework that analyzes error sources (backpropagation, truncation, shot noise) and selects the measurement protocol by comparing the cost scaling of QWC grouping versus derandomization bounds.
model_or_system: The work is applied to quantum computing circuits, tested on models like the XYZ Heisenberg Hamiltonian, QAOA, Ising, and QFT circuits, relevant for near-term quantum devices.
key_observables: Expectation values of observables ($\langle O angle$), backpropagated observables (linear combinations of Pauli observables), and the measurement cost (number of required measurements).
important_parameters: Desired accuracy ($\epsilon$), number of QWC groups ($N_{QWC}$), and the scaling factor related to Pauli weights ($\log(L) \cdot \max_{\ell} 3^{w(O_\ell)}$).
main_assumptions: The number of backpropagated observables can grow exponentially, necessitating truncation strategies (coefficient-based or Pauli-weight-based).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comprehensive framework for protocol selection, analyze the distribution of Pauli weights, and show performance comparisons (including noisy results) across various circuit families (QAOA, Ising, QFT) using the OBP-Derandomization protocol.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the unified framework, analyzes error sources, compares measurement protocols (QWC vs. Derandomization), and provides case studies on various Hamiltonians to determine the optimal measurement strategy.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous, resource-aware guidelines for running variational quantum algorithms, which is crucial for designing practical quantum circuits that minimize measurement overhead.
